html:
SMTO-SKL-0041 — Your Google account isn't a member of this shared drive

GUID: 3e0e141c-6a54-5001-a1ef-f0f9d6dba9e6
Slug: google-drive-shared-drive-not-authorized
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • The file or folder is in a shared drive, and the Google account SMTO used isn't a member of it, so Google refused the request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Google Drive with the account SMTO used and check whether the shared drive appears under Shared drives. If it isn't there, this account isn't a member.
  2. If another of your connected Google accounts is a member, tell SMTO to use that account for this request. Google only lets members of a shared drive see or change what's inside it.
  3. Otherwise, ask the shared drive's manager to add your account as a member with the access you need. Only a manager of the shared drive can grant membership.

What success looks like

  • The shared drive appears when you ask SMTO to list shared drives, and the request completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask for manager-level access if you only need to read files.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Drive returned HTTP 403 with reason teamDriveMembershipRequired for the selected account.

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 403 with teamDriveMembershipRequired. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 403 with teamDriveMembershipRequired.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact drive and selected account's membership.

How to fix it

  • provider_error mapped 403 teamDriveMembershipRequired to shared_drive_not_authorized. Choose an account_ref whose identity is a member of the shared drive with the needed role, or have a shared-drive manager add that account; confirm with google_drive.drives under the intended account.
  • Choose an authorized account and verify shared drive membership.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose an authorized account and verify shared drive membership.

How to verify the fix

  • An intentionally authorized account has the required shared-drive access.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
